The electric drive system comprises: an inverter unit (100) configured to convert externally supplied DC power into AC power; an electric motor unit (300) configured to convert the power supplied from the inverter unit (100) into mechanical rotation and to output the mechanical rotation via an output shaft (303); and a gearbox unit (200) configured to decelerate rotation transmitted from an input shaft (202) and to output the decelerated rotation. outputs.L2: Disclosed are a vehicle electric propulsion system and a motor vehicle equipped with that system. The electric drive system includes an inverter unit (100), which is arranged to change DC electricity supplied from an external source into AC electricity; an electric motor unit (300), which receives the electrical power from the inverter unit (100), converts it into mechanical rotational motion, and delivers that rotation through an output shaft (303); and a gearbox unit (200), which reduces the rotational speed received through an input shaft (202) and outputs the slowed rotation. The electric motor unit (300), the gearbox unit (200), and the inverter unit (100) each have their own separate housing. These three units are removably joined to one another along the axial direction of the gearbox unit input shaft (202), with the gearbox unit (200) arranged between the electric motor unit (300) and the inverter unit (100). outputs.L3:
The described technology relates to an electric drive system for a motor vehicle, as well as to a motor vehicle equipped with such an electric drive system.

The electric drive system includes an inverter unit, an electric motor unit, and a gearbox unit. The inverter unit is configured to receive externally supplied direct-current power and convert that direct-current power into alternating-current power suitable for driving the electric motor. The electric motor unit receives the alternating-current power supplied from the inverter unit and converts the electrical power into mechanical rotational power. This rotational power is transmitted through an output shaft of the electric motor unit.

The gearbox unit is arranged to receive the rotational power from the electric motor unit through an input shaft. The gearbox unit reduces, or decelerates, the speed of the received rotation and outputs the reduced rotational speed as drive power. In this way, the gearbox adjusts the rotational output of the motor to a speed and torque suitable for driving the vehicle.

The electric motor unit, the gearbox unit, and the inverter unit are each provided with their own independent enclosures. These units are detachably connected to one another in an axial direction, allowing the units to be assembled and separated as individual modules. In the connected state, the gearbox unit is positioned between the electric motor unit and the inverter unit. This arrangement provides a modular electric drive system in which the main functional units can be individually manufactured, assembled, serviced, or replaced while forming a compact axial drive configuration for a motor vehicle.
outputs.L4:
An electric drive system for a motor vehicle is provided. The electric drive system includes an electric motor, an inverter configured to supply electrical power to the electric motor, and a gearbox configured to transmit torque from the electric motor to a driven member of the vehicle. The motor, inverter, and gearbox are each arranged as separate, independently enclosed units. More particularly, the electric motor is received in a motor enclosure, the inverter is received in an inverter enclosure, and the gearbox is received in a gearbox enclosure. These enclosures are detachably connected to one another so that the individual units may be assembled, removed, serviced, or replaced independently.

The units are arranged along a common axial direction of the drive system. In this arrangement, the gearbox is positioned axially between the electric motor and the inverter. The motor enclosure is connected to one axial side of the gearbox enclosure, while the inverter enclosure is connected to an opposite axial side of the gearbox enclosure. The gearbox therefore forms an intermediate structural module between the motor and the inverter. This arrangement allows the drive system to be constructed as a compact modular assembly in which the main functional components are mechanically joined in series along the axial direction.

The electric motor may include a rotor and a stator disposed within the motor enclosure. The rotor is coupled to an input element of the gearbox, either directly or through an intermediate shaft or coupling. The gearbox may include one or more gear stages for adapting the speed and torque output of the motor to the requirements of the vehicle drivetrain. The gearbox output may be connected to a differential, axle shaft, wheel hub, or other torque-transmitting component of the motor vehicle.

The inverter is configured to convert electrical energy supplied from a vehicle energy source, such as a high-voltage battery, into a form suitable for driving the electric motor. The inverter may include power electronics, switching devices, control circuitry, bus bars, cooling structures, and electrical terminals arranged within the inverter enclosure. Electrical connections may extend from the inverter to the motor, preferably through or adjacent to the gearbox region, while maintaining the independent enclosure of each module.

Because the inverter enclosure is located on the side of the gearbox opposite the motor, the inverter does not need to be arranged radially around the motor or integrated into the motor housing. Instead, the inverter may be formed as a relatively thin axial module. The inverter enclosure can therefore be minimized in axial thickness while still providing sufficient space for the power electronics and associated electrical connections. Reducing the axial thickness of the inverter enclosure contributes to a reduction in the overall axial length of the drive system.

The detachable connection between the motor enclosure, gearbox enclosure, and inverter enclosure provides several advantages. Each unit may be manufactured and tested separately before final assembly. Different motors, gearboxes, or inverters may be combined to form drive systems with different performance characteristics while using a common modular architecture. Maintenance and repair are also simplified, since a defective unit may be removed and replaced without requiring replacement of the entire drive assembly.

The positioning of the gearbox between the motor and inverter further enables efficient packaging within the vehicle. The gearbox enclosure can serve as a central supporting structure for the drive system, with the motor and inverter mounted to opposite sides. This reduces the need for additional mounting brackets or connecting structures and can improve stiffness of the assembly. The compact axial arrangement is particularly advantageous in vehicles where installation space is limited, such as electric or hybrid vehicles with highly integrated drive modules.

In one embodiment, the motor enclosure, gearbox enclosure, and inverter enclosure are connected by releasable fasteners, such as bolts or screws, extending through corresponding flange portions. Sealing elements may be provided between adjacent enclosures to prevent ingress of moisture, dust, or other contaminants. Cooling passages may be provided in one or more of the enclosures, and the cooling system may be arranged so that the motor, gearbox, and inverter can be thermally managed either separately or in combination.

Overall, the described electric drive system provides a compact, modular, and serviceable drive assembly for a motor vehicle. By arranging independently enclosed inverter, motor, and gearbox units in the axial direction and positioning the gearbox between the motor and inverter, the system achieves a space-saving configuration. The minimized axial thickness of the inverter enclosure further reduces the total package size of the drive system while preserving modularity and ease of assembly.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an electric drive system for a motor vehicle, including an inverter unit, motor unit, and gearbox unit arranged axially with separate detachable enclosures.
counterfactuals.output: An electric drive system for a motor vehicle includes an inverter unit, a motor unit, and a gearbox unit arranged successively along a common axial direction. The inverter unit, the motor unit, and the gearbox unit are each received in a respective enclosure, wherein the enclosures are formed as separate housing components detachably connected to one another. The motor unit includes an electric machine having a rotor coupled to an input side of the gearbox unit, and the inverter unit is electrically connected to stator windings of the electric machine for supplying drive power thereto. The detachable enclosures define independent installation spaces for the inverter unit, motor unit, and gearbox unit, enabling modular assembly, service, and replacement of the units while maintaining axial alignment of the drive train. Mechanical interfaces, electrical interfaces, and sealing interfaces between adjacent enclosures are configured to permit releasable connection and separation of the units without destruction of the respective enclosures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the following invention in one paragraph using patent claim language: an EV drive assembly where the gearbox is between the motor and inverter, all three housings are independent and detachable, and the inverter housing is thinnest axially.
counterfactuals.output: An electric vehicle drive assembly comprising an electric motor, a gearbox, and an inverter arranged along an axial direction, wherein a gearbox housing is disposed between a motor housing of the electric motor and an inverter housing of the inverter, the motor housing, gearbox housing, and inverter housing being separate, independent housings configured to be detachably coupled to one another, and wherein the inverter housing has an axial thickness less than an axial thickness of each of the motor housing and the gearbox housing.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical description of an electric vehicle drivetrain comprising inverter unit 100, gearbox unit 200, and electric motor unit 300, emphasizing their axial arrangement and enclosure configuration.
counterfactuals.output:
An electric vehicle drivetrain includes an inverter unit 100, a gearbox unit 200, and an electric motor unit 300 arranged sequentially along a common axial direction. The electric motor unit 300 is coupled to the gearbox unit 200 to transmit rotational power through a reduction gear or transmission mechanism, while the inverter unit 100 is electrically connected to the electric motor unit 300 to supply controlled drive current.

The gearbox unit 200 is positioned axially between the inverter unit 100 and the electric motor unit 300, forming a compact integrated drive assembly. Each unit may include a dedicated housing portion, or the units may be accommodated within a common enclosure structure having partitioned compartments. The enclosure supports alignment of the motor shaft and gearbox input/output components, provides mechanical protection, and may define integrated mounting, sealing, cooling, and electrical connection features for the inverter, gearbox, and motor units.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an English patent abstract for a motor vehicle electric drive system in which DC power is converted to AC, the motor outputs rotation through shaft 303, the gearbox reduces speed through input shaft 202, and the units are detachably connected.
counterfactuals.output: An electric drive system for a motor vehicle includes a drive unit and a gearbox unit detachably connected to one another. The drive unit includes an inverter configured to convert DC power supplied from a power source into AC power, and an electric motor configured to receive the AC power and generate rotational output through a motor output shaft. The gearbox unit includes an input shaft configured to be coupled to the motor output shaft, the input shaft transmitting the rotational output to a speed reduction mechanism that reduces the rotational speed and outputs driving torque to a vehicle drive member. The motor output shaft may be shaft 303, and the gearbox input shaft may be input shaft 202. The detachable connection between the drive unit and the gearbox unit enables separate assembly, maintenance, replacement, or adaptation of the drive unit and gearbox unit while maintaining mechanical power transmission between the motor and the gearbox.
